title: 02 demands a rejection the LRM contradicts by printing the identical construct as its own worked example — a conforming compiler fails it
detail:
VERIFIED. 02_user_systf_function_call.va asserts `//! reject $fixture_vpi_gain` on `analog I(p,n) <+ $fixture_vpi_gain(V(p,n));`. docs/VAMS-LRM/ch12-vpi-routines.html §12.32.3 prints exactly that shape as the LRM's own example of vpi_register_analog_systf(): `module sampnhold(out,in); electrical out,in; parameter real period = 1e-3; analog begin V(out) <+ $sampler(V(in), period); end endmodule`. §2.8.3 (verified in ch2-lexical.html) makes `$name` grammatical and lists five definition sites, the fourth being 'defined using the VPI as described in Clause 11 and Clause 12'; §12.31.4 gives cbUnresolvedSystf as the host's disposition for an unresolved one. Nothing requires a compiler to reject it. The fixture's own header concedes this: 'DEBT - this rejection is NOT conformance. The LRM permits what VerA refuses here.'

The expectation is also the weakest possible. torture.zig:634 `failureContains` matches a non-code substring against `f.generated` — the ENTIRE generated Zig text — so `//! reject $fixture_vpi_gain` is satisfied by the callee name appearing anywhere in the emitted device, including the source echo in the @compileError. Any error whatsoever passes it.

Merges with the second half of the same defect: §12.32.3's sampnhold is the chapter's second (and only other) normative .va snippet and has NO fixture anywhere in the tree (grep for sampler/sampnhold across tests/fixtures returns only an unrelated prose comment in ch07_mixed_signal/analog_event.va). One file fixes both: replace 02's invented `$fixture_vpi_gain` module with the LRM's verbatim sampnhold.

VERIFIED VerA behavior (`vera --emit-zig` on the verbatim sampnhold): 'codegen refused a construct; the generated device contains @compileError'. Identical refusal to today's 02, so the rename changes the file's meaning, not its verdict.

ENCODING WARNING — do NOT take the `weak` lens's proposed fix (`//! lrm 2.8.3 + //! reject E0512 + //! xfail`). Per tests/fixtures/README.md:175-208 and torture.zig:550, `//! xfail` means 'the LRM says this is an error and VerA fails to diagnose it', and when the reject substrings DO match the runner reports XPASS as a hard FAIL. Here the polarity is inverted: the LRM permits the construct and VerA refuses it. `reject`+`xfail` writes the requirement backwards. The runner has no verdict for 'must compile, VerA cannot' — `refused`/CANNOT RUN is reserved for the contract.validate num_ports case (torture.zig:149-158).

title: 45 reject fixtures pin §4.7, carry zero //! lrm, and wear chapter-12 filenames for a rule chapter 12 does not state
detail:
VERIFIED. Files 03-47 are one template repeated 45 times: `//! reject E0512` / `//! reject vpi_<name>` / `// EXPECT: error` / `analog I(p,n) <+ vpi_<name>(0);`. `grep -l '//! lrm' *.va` = 0 across all 47 files; the contract in tests/fixtures/README.md makes the cite mandatory on every reject fixture.

The rule they pin is not in chapter 12. `vpi_get` etc. are ordinary identifiers — `grep -ci vpi_ docs/VAMS-LRM/annex-b-keywords.html` = 0, so nothing is reserved. VerA's own catalogue agrees: src/diag_code.zig:1575-1577 gives E0512 `.title = "unknown function"`, `.lrm = "4.7"`. Confirmed live: `vera` on `analog I(p,n) <+ fixture_vpi_gain(V(p,n));` emits `error[E0512]: unknown function` with `= note: LRM 4.7`. The rejection is CORRECT; the attribution is not.

Also folds in the vestigial third oracle: `// EXPECT: error` is line 3 of all 45, is a plain comment (torture.zig parses only `//!`), and reads like an expectation while enforcing nothing.

A reviewer may reasonably prefer the `negatives` lens's harder call — delete all 45 and keep ONE honestly-cited fixture in ch04_expressions — since 45 copies of one §4.7 test is dead weight. Retagging is the smaller diff and loses nothing; either way the `//! lrm 12.x` cite must NOT be fabricated. Land item ch12-5 (duplicate deletion) first so this pass touches 35 files, not 45.

title: 34 COVERAGE.md rows claim a chapter-12 section is 'rejected by' a fixture that pins §4.7, and s12-32-3 is mapped to a fixture of a different construct
detail:
VERIFIED by count: 34 rows of the form 'Host C routine boundary; direct Verilog-A misuse is rejected by `NN_xxx_not_va.va`' (the `uncovered` lens said 33 — off by one; `weak` said 34, correct). Every one of those fixtures pins §4.7, per item ch12-2, so the rows are 34 fake coverage entries.

Three further specific falsehoods in the file:
  - `s12-32-3` reads 'Registration/derivative examples are C-only; LRM `.va` call form is `01`' — but §12.32.3's .va snippet is the sampnhold/$sampler analog system FUNCTION in expression position, and 01 is §12.22.2's $resistor analog system TASK in statement position. Different construct, different half of the API (calltf-only vs derivtf).
  - `s12-22-2` implies the numeric content of §12.22.2 is covered by 01. It is not and cannot be: the conductance `g = 1.0/r` and `arg1 := V(p,n)*g` live in resistor_calltf(), reachable only through a linked VPI host. Say so instead of naming a fixture.
  - The header says representative misuse fixtures 03-13 'require a loud unknown call diagnostic', presenting a §4.7 diagnostic as chapter-12 coverage.

Also record the negatives census, which VERIFIES as a non-finding worth writing down once: an exhaustive prohibition grep of ch12 yields 12 hits, ZERO source-facing — three are anti-prohibitions ('shall NOT be an error to cancel an event'), the rest bind a C application. No `//! reject` fixture is derivable from Clause 12. That sentence replaces the implication that 45 sections are 'rejected by' something.
expected:
Replace the 34 'rejected by' rows with one row per C-only section reading 'C ABI; no Verilog-A source obligation. The `NN_*_not_va.va` fixture pins §4.7, not this section.'

Add, once, near the top: 'Clause 12 contains no prohibition that Verilog-AMS source text can violate; no //! reject fixture is derivable from it.'

Fix `s12-22-2` to state the numeric semantics require a registered VPI host and are out of reach of a .va suite. Fix `s12-32-3` to name the sampnhold fixture from item ch12-1, or 'uncovered' if that item lands as a deletion.

Regenerate the literal fixture inventory after items ch12-1 and ch12-5.

title: The chapter's only running fixture asserts a §2.6.1 scale factor, verbatim duplicating ch02_lexical/07 — nothing about §12.22.2 is observed
detail:
VERIFIED. 01's sole assertion is `CHECKX("1k scale factor on the systf argument", r, 1000.0)` against `parameter real r = 1k`. That is the chapter-2 SI rule and it is already asserted with the same want at tests/fixtures/ch02_lexical/07_si_scale_factors.va:24 — `CHECKX("k is 1e3 as well", 1k, 1000.0)`. The literals lens confirms the number itself is right (Table 2-1 k = 1e3, exact in double, CHECKX is the correct macro) — there is no literal defect here, only a misplaced one. The assertion is insensitive to the construct under test: with or without a VPI host the verdict is identical, so a compiler that has never heard of §12.22.2 passes.

Two claims ARE reachable from source with no host, and I ran them: with `integer seq;` set to 1 before `$resistor(current, V(p,n), r)` and `seq = seq + 2` after, `vera --run` prints `block continues past an unregistered analog system task got=3 want=3 ok=1` and `no calltf ran, so the output argument is untouched got=0 want=0 ok=1`. Both pass today and both are chapter-12 facts: the block runs straight through an unregistered analog system task (§5.3.1 sequencing over the §12.22.2 call form), and with no calltf nothing is written to the output argument.

Dropping the CHECKX line is not optional — its presence disguises an unasserted fixture as a passing one.

title: 10 of the 45 reject fixtures duplicate a fixture in the same directory — same callee, same rule, same code
detail:
VERIFIED by callee census over the directory: exactly 10 vpi_ callee names appear twice — vpi_get_str (04 == 23), vpi_handle_by_name (05 == 32), vpi_iterate (06 == 34), vpi_get_delays (07 == 22), vpi_get_analog_value (08 == 21), vpi_get_analog_time (09 == 20), vpi_register_cb (10 == 42), vpi_register_analog_systf (11 == 43), vpi_mcd_open (12 == 37), vpi_sim_control (13 == 47).

Correction to the `negatives` lens: they are NOT all byte-for-byte identical — the 03-13 batch sometimes uses a different arity (`vpi_get_str(1, 0)` vs `vpi_get_str(0)`, `vpi_iterate(1, 0)` vs `vpi_iterate(0)`). Arity is irrelevant: E0512 fires on name resolution and never reaches the argument list, so they are semantic duplicates as the `weak` lens states. The unit of work is unchanged.

03_chk_error_not_va.va is the only member of the 03-13 batch with a unique callee (vpi_chk_error) and must be KEPT. Do this before item ch12-2 so the retag pass touches 35 files instead of 45.
expected: Delete the 10 listed .va files and their .expected-error.txt sidecars. Keep 03_chk_error_not_va.va and the whole 14-47 atomic series. Drop the 10 rows from COVERAGE.md's literal fixture inventory (folded into item ch12-3).

title: A systf name may repeat freely across call sites — no fixture in the tree calls one $name more than once
detail:
VERIFIED in the LRM: §12.32 states 'The task or function name shall be unique in the domain in which it is registered. That is, the same name can be shared by two sets of callbacks, provided that one set is registered in the digital domain and the other is registered in the analog.' Uniqueness is a property of the REGISTRATION, not of the source — a `$name` may appear at any number of call sites.

The compiler-side failure this catches is real and common: a compiler that interns `$name` on first sight and diagnoses the second occurrence as a redefinition, or that binds two call sites to one entity. Every existing fixture in ch12 and ch11 calls its `$name` exactly once, so nothing discriminates.

VERIFIED runnable today: a module with two `$fixture_vpi_task(...)` calls in one analog block, different arguments, `seq = 1 / +2 / +4`, compiles clean (rc=0) and `vera --run` prints `repeated call sites of one systf name are not a redefinition got=7 want=7 ok=1`. This is a plain run fixture, not a reject and not an xfail — nothing in the LRM makes a repeated call site an error, so a compiler that diagnoses one must fail here.

Use the statement position (analog system TASK), not expression position: expression position hits VerA's codegen refusal (item ch12-1) and would drown the rule under an unrelated limitation.

title: 46 .expected-error.txt sidecars survive in a directory whose README opens with 'No sidecar files'
detail:
VERIFIED count: 46 sidecars beside 47 .va (the `negatives` lens said 47 — off by one; `weak` said 46, correct; 01 has none). tests/fixtures/README.md:3 states the contract as '859 .va files. One runner, tests/torture.zig. No sidecar files' and :5-7 'there is no second file to drift out of step with it.'

Safe to delete: the only reader is tests/conformance.zig:97-98, and conformance.zig is no longer a build step — build.zig:69 mentions it only in a comment saying torture 'replaced conformance, exhaustive, sema.sh and ledger'. The runner is dead code and the sidecars are its dead oracle.

They have already drifted, exactly as the contract predicts: 02_user_systf_function_call.expected-error.txt asserts 'a user systf has no compile-time definition, so it must be refused rather than faked', which flatly contradicts the .va header's 'the LRM permits what VerA refuses here'. Every substring the 46 carry (E0512 + the callee name) is already present in the corresponding .va as `//! reject` lines.
expected: rm tests/fixtures/ch12_vpi_routines/*.expected-error.txt. Do this after items ch12-1 and ch12-5 so the deletions do not overlap. Consider deleting tests/conformance.zig in the same commit — it is unreferenced by build.zig.

title: `//! reject vpi_get` is a prefix of 13 other callee names in the same directory
detail:
VERIFIED: `vpi_get` is a strict prefix of vpi_get_str, vpi_get_value, vpi_get_time, vpi_get_delays, vpi_get_real, vpi_get_cb_info, vpi_get_vlog_info, vpi_get_systf_info, vpi_get_analog_delta, vpi_get_analog_freq, vpi_get_analog_time, vpi_get_analog_value and vpi_get_analog_systf_info — all present in this directory. Made worse by torture.zig:634, which matches a non-code substring against the whole generated text, not just the diagnostic message.

Harmless today because `//! reject E0512` is also required and the file contains a single call, but it is the one substring in the set that does not pin the callee it names, and the pattern must not be copied. One character fixes it. Fold into the item ch12-2 pass rather than a separate commit.
